properties.name: governance.http-logging.async
properties.description: If true (the default), publishing the captured HttpAccessLogEvent is handed off to a bounded background executor instead of running on the request thread - the response is sent without waiting on whatever the configured HttpAccessLogPublisher does. Set false to force synchronous publishing (the event is guaranteed published before the request completes) at the cost of the publish call adding to request latency.

properties.name: governance.http-logging.enabled
properties.description: Master switch. Defaults to true - opt-out, not opt-in, like the rest of the suite.

properties.name: governance.http-logging.excluded-paths
properties.description: Paths excluded from logging entirely, e.g. health checks and the actuator tree.

properties.name: governance.http-logging.include-body
properties.description: Log request/response bodies. Off by default: bodies are the highest PII/PCI risk surface.

properties.name: governance.http-logging.include-params
properties.description: Log the request's query string and request parameters (query string + form-encoded body params, per the servlet spec's getParameterMap()). On by default - query params/request params are a lower PII/PCI risk surface than full bodies (most sensitive data belongs in a body or header, not a URL - putting it in a URL is itself bad practice), but sensitive values are still masked per sensitiveParameterNames below.

properties.name: governance.http-logging.max-body-size
properties.description: Max number of body characters captured/logged, to bound log line size and memory use.

properties.name: governance.http-logging.sample-rate
properties.description: Fraction of requests actually logged, 0.0-1.0. Lets high-throughput payment-processing services keep governance enabled but sample instead of logging every single call. 1.0 (log everything) by default.

properties.name: governance.http-logging.sensitive-body-fields
properties.description: JSON field names masked (regex, name-based) inside captured request/response bodies. Raw HTTP bodies aren't annotated Java objects, so field-level @Sensitive can't apply here directly - this is the name-based equivalent, and the reason includeBody defaults to false: this is a best-effort net, not a guarantee, for arbitrary/nested/array JSON shapes.

properties.name: governance.http-logging.sensitive-header-strategy
properties.description: Masking strategy applied to any header name in sensitiveHeaders.

properties.name: governance.http-logging.sensitive-headers
properties.description: Header names treated as sensitive and masked with the given strategy regardless of includeHeaders - name-matched case-insensitively.

properties.name: governance.http-logging.sensitive-parameter-names
properties.description: Query-string/request-parameter NAMES masked with sensitiveHeaderStrategy whenever captured (name-matched case-insensitively) - separate from sensitiveBodyFields since these are plain key=value pairs, not JSON.

properties.name: management.endpoint.governance-http-logging.access
properties.description: Permitted level of access for the governanceHttpLogging endpoint.

properties.name: management.endpoint.governance-http-logging.cache.time-to-live
properties.description: Maximum time that a response can be cached.

properties.name: management.endpoint.governance-http-logging.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable the governanceHttpLogging endpoint.
